name: Myrel, Shield of Argive
oracle_text:
During your turn, your opponents can't cast spells or activate abilities of artifacts, creatures, or enchantments.
Whenever Myrel attacks, create X 1/1 colorless Soldier artifact creature tokens, where X is the number of Soldiers you control.
blocked_sentences: During your turn, your opponents can't cast spells or activate abilities of artifacts, creatures, or enchantments.
Whenever Myrel attacks, create X 1/1 colorless Soldier artifact creature tokens, where X is the number of Soldiers you control.

needs.what: A player-wide static that stops the named players ACTIVATING abilities of permanents matched by a printed-characteristics filter, for as long as its optional `condition` holds -- Grand Abolisher's second half, and Myrel's. Suggested shape: a `static_effects` entry such as `cant_activate_abilities` taking `affects_player` ("you" / "opponent" / "any"), an optional `condition` (here `{"is_your_turn": true}`, answered by `_active_player_statics` exactly as `cant_cast_spells` already answers it) and an optional `affects` filter over printed characteristics (here `{"any_types": ["Artifact", "Creature", "Enchantment"]}`, from `static_filter_keys`). Unlike `cant_cast_spells` the filter is REQUIRED vocabulary rather than a refusable extra, because every printed card in this family names permanent types: Grand Abolisher says "artifacts, creatures, or enchantments", so shipping the effect filterless would stop opponents' lands and planeswalkers too. It needs a new predicate beside `player_cant_cast_spells` in src/automtg/engine/player_statics.py:1093 that takes the OBJECT as well as the player -- `player_cant_activate(state, pid, oid)` -- read in src/automtg/engine/legality.py:491 `_activate_actions`, in the same `continue` that already drops `obj.abilities_locked` at line 497, and again in the mana solver, for the reason src/automtg/engine/objects.py:1122 gives about `abilities_locked`: a locked permanent that still taps for mana makes the lock worthless. 605.1a/602.5d mean mana abilities are caught too, since the printed line excepts nothing, but the filter keeps lands out by type. It also has to be asked at the same three resolution-time seams `player_cant_cast_spells` is (101.2: a "can't" beats a "may"), so an opponent's trigger cannot offer an activation past it. This unblocks the whole Abolisher family at once: Grand Abolisher, Myrel, Shield of Argive, Dosan's twins, Conqueror's Flail and Teferi, Time Raveler's neighbours.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `cant_cast_spells` is the near miss and is explicitly only half the sentence: its own docstring (src/automtg/engine/player_statics.py:1105-1110) lists what it does NOT stop -- "copying a spell, **activating abilities**, playing a land, and the special actions suspend and foretell" -- and closes with "Grand Abolisher's second half is a different static". Its loader guard at src/automtg/cards/loader/__init__.py:3239 also refuses an `affects` filter on it, so it cannot even carry the "of artifacts, creatures, or enchantments" half; writing the line as `cant_cast_spells` alone drops a printed clause, which is the approximation the brief forbids. `lock_abilities` is the other near relative and gates the wrong axis three times over: it is an OP, so it can only run once from a resolving spell or trigger and cannot be Myrel's ongoing static; it is recorded as an until-end-of-turn `TempEffect` (src/automtg/engine/primitives.py:1565) that the cleanup step drops, so it could not last "during your turn" let alone re-apply each of the controller's turns; and it names a fixed set of object ids at resolution, so a permanent an opponent plays afterwards is untouched. `detain` is the same shape and expires at the next untap. `lose_all_abilities` is strictly wider and permanent -- it removes triggered, static and mana abilities as well, so the opponent's Sol Ring would stop making mana even on their own turn. `ability_cost_reduction` and `attack_tax` are prices, not prohibitions: no number stops an activation the way "can't" does. Nothing in `static_effects` prohibits an activation at all, and no `condition_keys`/`static_condition_keys` entry could bolt one onto an unrelated effect. The card's second sentence is blocked separately (see below), so no partial answer was written.

needs.what: The token id for a **1/1 colorless Soldier artifact creature token** -- `types: ["Artifact", "Creature"]`, `subtypes: ["Soldier"]`, `colors: []`, 1/1 -- added to data/cards/tokens.cards.json as, say, `soldier_1_1_c_artifact`. This is the Phyrexia/Brothers' War-era Soldier token printed by Myrel, Shield of Argive, Mishra's Foundry, Thran Spider and the rest of that cycle. With it in the pool the second sentence is otherwise fully expressible today and needs no engine work: an `attacks` trigger whose `create_token` carries `amount: {"count": {"zone": "battlefield", "controller": "you", "subtypes": ["Soldier"]}}` says "X is the number of Soldiers you control" exactly, and the tokens count themselves for the NEXT attack because they are Soldiers too.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `token_ids` is a closed list and holds no colorless artifact Soldier. The two Soldier tokens that exist are both wrong cards: `soldier_1_1_w` (data/cards/isperia.cards.json:1361) is a 1/1 WHITE Soldier creature and `human_soldier_1_1_w` (data/cards/tokens.cards.json) is a 1/1 white Human Soldier creature -- neither is an artifact and neither is colorless, which is the whole point of the token on a commander whose deck counts artifacts: substituting one would silently break every artifact count, every metalcraft/affinity-style payoff, improvise, and any "colorless" or "nonwhite" check, and would add a spurious Human for tribal effects. The three colorless artifact creature tokens that do exist are each a different creature type and so miss the Soldier count this very card reads: `gnome_1_1_c` is a Gnome, `thopter_1_1_c_flying` is a 1/1 Thopter WITH FLYING, and `construct_0_0_c_artifact_buff` is a 0/0 Construct with its own printed ability. `hero_1_1_c` and `spirit_1_1_c` are 1/1 colorless but are not artifacts and are not Soldiers. `create_token` has no key that recolours, retypes or renames the token it names -- `op_options` for it is amount/as/attached_to/attacking/controller/or_planeswalker/player/tapped/token -- and `add_subtype` after the fact would not make the existing white Soldier colorless or an artifact, would be a separate continuous effect, and would still leave the token white for the turn it was made. Per the packet's own note this is a one-line data change and the cheapest gap in the pipeline to close.
